newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-WOOSNAM AND PRICE SHARE MILLION DOLLAR LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOOSNAM AND PRICE SHARE MILLION DOLLAR LEAD.

text.p: Welshman Ian Woosnam missed a six-foot birdie putt at the 18th and had to settle for a share of the third-round lead with Zimbabwe's Nick Price in the Million Dollar Challenge on Saturday.
Woosnam, the 1987 champion, produced immaculate golf from tee to green to card a five-under-par 67 for a 54-hole total of 204 - 12-under for the tournament.
Price, the 1993 winner, was less consistent but putted superbly as he fired eight birdies in a six-under-par 66, the low round of the day.

European number one and overnight leader Colin Montgomerie struggled with his iron play as he carded a two-under-par 70, surrendering the lead to Woosnam as early as the third hole as he dropped to fourth place in the 12-man field.
U.S. Open champion Steve Jones recovered from a bogey at the first to shoot 67, helped by an eagle three at the 10th as he took over third spot.

Woosnam, despite his persistent back trouble, made the early running and had a two-shot lead after an outward nine of 31 with five birdies coming from good iron shots close to the pin. He could have secured a sixth had he holed a 10-foot putt at the ninth.

Not even three wasp stings on his left calf at the par-three seventh could disturb the European number two's concentration. Having removed the offending insect from his left trouser leg, he coolly sank a 12-foot putt for his fourth bidie of the round.
He was generally happy with his round, but is still searching for a more suitable driver.

"I'm pretty happy with my game but my driving was my worst enemy today," Woosnam said. "I'm still looking for a driver that suits me. But I'm hitting my irons so well that today it was better to use my one iron off the tee and then hit into the greens with longer irons."
Price, the former world number one who is looking for his first tournament win of the year, was overjoyed to rediscover his putting touch after an indirect tip from South African Ernie Els.

"Today was the best I've putted since I can remember," he said. "Last night I watched Ernie's putting posture on the television highlights of the second round and I tried to keep my back straight on the putting green this morning.
"It seemed to work. I got more and more confident with my putting today as I went on. And, as I sank more putts, I was getting more confidence with the irons."
